summary: M1 MacBook DEP re-enroll fails: third-party kext blocks MDM profile & cert install after depot repair
description:
Issue summary:
After depot repair (logic board replacement) of Apple Silicon MacBooks, several devices fail to complete DEP/MDM re-enrollment during OOBE. The MDM profile push stalls and the SSO cert/profile does not install. A third-party kernel extension (legacy VPN client kext) is present on the image and appears to intercept network stack initialization during first-boot, preventing MDM from completing.

Impact:
- ~6 devices failed re-enroll in the last week after depot repairs; devices remain unmanaged and cannot receive corporate certs/policies.
- Affected users are blocked from corporate VPN and SSO until manual remediation.

Context/Notes:
- All affected units are Apple Silicon (M1/M2) models returned from repair with a replaced system board.
- Image includes a legacy enterprise VPN that installs a kernel extension for older macOS versions; the kext is code-signed but not notarized for Apple Silicon-specific requirements.
- On Intel Macs this did not present at scale; appears tied to kext load order and the new hardware IDs after logic board swap.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use depot repair flow; replace logic board on M1 MacBook and restore company image via DEP image tool.
2) Boot device into OOBE with network available (corporate Wi-Fi or ethernet via dock).
3) Device checks in with DEP, Apple MDM push begins but stalls on profile installation step 'com.redwood.mdm:install-profile'.
4) Observe that sysdiagnose shows kernel extension related logs and the mdm-agent log shows repeated network initialization failures.
observed_behavior: DEP check-in completes but MDM profile push stalls. mdm-agent repeatedly logs: 'network stack init failed - interface not ready' and macOS kernel reports 'kext com.company.vpn attempted unsupported operations on Apple Silicon'.
expected_behavior: Device should complete DEP/MDM re-enroll automatically during OOBE, install SSO certs and corporate profiles without manual intervention.
logs: mdm-agent: 2024-11-15T09:12:17Z ERROR network: interface not ready
kernel: Nov 15 09:12:16 kextd[54]: com.company.vpn: attempted to register deprecated network filter (not supported on arm64e)
system.log excerpt: DEP: token validated, pushing profiles (profileID=com.redwood.sso) - stalled at 98%
investigation_notes: Initial triage by mac-ops: reproduced on staging image with legacy VPN kext present.
Disabling the VPN kext prior to OOBE (via post-image script that removes the kext bundle) allows MDM to complete normally.
Kext is signed by vendor but not notarized for M1-specific requirements; notarization warning appears in kext load messages.
Hypothesis: on new system board hardware IDs, the kext attempts a network-level hook earlier in boot and blocks system network interfaces until degraded, causing mdm-agent timeouts.
Checked DEP portal: device records are correct; no Apple-side MDM flags indicate block.
comments: Priya Nair (mac-ops): 'I can reproduce on MBP18,1 with the vendor kext present. Removing the kext before runbook upload fixes enrollment. Need to confirm scope of devices with this kext.'
Aaron Kim (SecOps): 'Vendor confirmed they have an M1-compatible signed driver but we require notarization and an updated installer that avoids early network hooks. Asking for vendor ETA.'
Jordan Lee (reporter): 'Opened INT ticket after 4 devices returned from repair this week failed. Will pause autopilot-like reassign workflows until remediation.'
resolution:
Workaround applied: depot imaging pipeline modified to detect and remove legacy VPN kexts on Apple Silicon builds prior to shipping. Mac-ops will reimage affected units and perform manual profile push where needed. Vendor engaged for notarized M1-friendly installer; security requested vendor PR to remove kernel-level hooks and move to NetworkExtension framework.

Follow-up actions:
- Ship a patched image by 2024-11-20 without legacy kexts for Apple Silicon fleet (assigned to mac-ops).
- Vendor action item logged; expect vendor ETA in 5 business days (tracked in related_github_pr).
- Add a post-repair verification step in depot runbook to validate MDM check-in within 10 minutes of OOBE.
resolution_notes: 2024-11-16: mac-ops rolled a temporary image removal step for kexts; 3/3 reimage attempts succeeded and devices checked into MDM.
2024-11-17: SecOps confirmed vendor engagement; vendor PR submitted to GitHub (see related_github_prs).
Follow-up ticket created to audit all Apple Silicon images for legacy kernel extensions (INT-1000457).
